title: Vanderbilt BIEN Lab SOZ Resting State SEEG Classification (processed resting-state SEEG)
description: Processed resting-state stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) recordings from 79 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy evaluated at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. Each patient contributed five minutes of awake, eyes-closed interictal data, stored as filtered bipolar-montage signals with region-level seizure onset zone (SOZ) labels. The data accompany a study that trains deep neural networks to classify SOZ versus non-SOZ brain regions from brief interictal recordings.
methods_description: Five minutes of awake, eyes-closed resting-state SEEG were recorded per patient, with at least 4 h separation from electroclinical activity. Signals were converted to a bipolar montage of adjacent contacts and filtered with zero-phase Butterworth filters (MATLAB filtfilt; passbands 1-59, 61-119 and 121-150 Hz). Contacts were localized on post-implantation CT and assigned to Desikan-Killiany regions. SOZs were defined per region.
